Question: Joey and his five brothers are ages \(3,\) \(5,\) \(7,\) \(9,\) \(11,\) and \(13.\) One afternoon two of his brothers whose ages sum to \(16\) went to the movies, two brothers younger than \(10\) went to play baseball, and Joey and the \(5\)-year-old stayed home. How old is Joey?
Solution:
The \(11\)- and \(13\)-year-olds are both too old to play baseball. They also cannot both go to the movies, since \(11+13=24\), not \(16\). Therefore at least one of them must stay home. The two people at home are Joey and the \(5\)-year-old, so Joey must be either \(11\) or \(13\).

If Joey were \(13\), the \(11\)-year-old would have to go to the movies. His movie partner would then need to be \(16-11=5\) years old, but the \(5\)-year-old stayed home. This is impossible.

Thus Joey is \(11\). This age works: the \(3\)- and \(13\)-year-olds go to the movies, the \(7\)- and \(9\)-year-olds play baseball, and Joey and the \(5\)-year-old stay home. Joey is \(\boxed{11}\) years old, choice D.
